cards.headline: PAP refreshing ideas, expanding networks to renew itself: PM Wong
bullets: PM Wong says the PAP will renew itself by refreshing ideas and expanding its networks.
The party aims to connect with more Singaporeans from different backgrounds and professions.
New ways for people to engage with the party include the 'Friends of the PAP' network.
PM Wong stressed that party renewal means making room for younger members while valuing veterans' experience.

cards.headline: Gas Supply may pursue remedies if contract breached following Indonesia’s export cuts: Tan See Leng
bullets: Gas Supply may seek legal options if Indonesia breaches contract over gas cuts.
Indonesia is cutting gas exports to Singapore by less than 2% of daily demand.
Singapore has enough gas from other sources, including liquefied natural gas.
Electricity prices unlikely to be affected much in the short term.
Singapore is building a second LNG terminal and diversifying energy sources.

cards.headline: New blood test could help flag risk of condition that leads to liver failure, cancer
bullets: A new Singapore-made blood test can spot early signs of liver cirrhosis risk.
The test, called CIRRHOClear, checks for specific signals in your blood.
It helps doctors find liver damage before symptoms show up.
This could help prevent liver failure and common liver cancer.
The test is for people aged 40 and above.

cards.headline: Institutions need to evolve to changing needs but core values, purpose should endure: Zaqy Mohamad
bullets: Institutions must adapt to new needs while keeping their core values, said Zaqy Mohamad.
He spoke at the opening of Jamae Chulia Heritage, a new development on endowment land.
The project turns old Muslim endowment property into a serviced residence and retail space.
This renewal keeps the original purpose of benefiting future generations, he noted.
Zaqy also highlighted Singapore's long history of diversity and openness.

cards.headline: WP’s position seems to shift with ‘political winds’, PAP must take wider view: PM Wong
bullets: PM Wong says Workers' Party changes its stand on issues like housing and foreign workers.
He pointed out the WP's different views on building new flats over the years.
Wong also noted the WP's shifting stance on foreign manpower policies.
He stated the PAP must consider long-term interests, unlike opposition parties.
PM Wong said it's easier to oppose when not in charge.

cards.headline: ‘Keep calm and carry on’: Indonesia gas cut unlikely to hit Singapore electricity prices, says Tan See Leng
bullets: Indonesia cutting gas exports to Singapore is unlikely to affect electricity prices here.
The cut amounts to less than 2% of Singapore's daily gas needs, with enough supply available.
Global gas prices are a bigger factor for Singapore's energy costs, not this specific cut.
Singapore has backup plans and diversified energy sources to ensure supply reliability.
Authorities are leaving contract remedies to Singapore's gas importer, Gas Supply Private Limited.

cards.headline: PAP votes in top decision-making body, Jeffrey Siow and Jasmin Lau nominated but not voted in
bullets: PAP elected its top decision-making body, the CEC, at its conference.
Lawrence Wong led the party's first CEC election since becoming PM.
First-term MPs Jeffrey Siow and Jasmin Lau were nominated but not elected.
Lawrence Wong stressed the need to earn continued support from Singaporeans.

cards.headline: Governing means confronting politically difficult issues, not just balancing interests: PM Wong
bullets: PM Wong says governing means tackling tough issues, not just balancing interests.
He warned against populism and offering easy answers to hard problems.
The PAP government must make unpopular decisions for Singapore's future.
Singapore is exploring nuclear energy and diversifying gas imports for energy security.

cards.headline: Singapore expects all parties to honour commercial gas contracts, says PM Wong after Indonesia cut exports
bullets: Indonesia cut gas exports to Singapore, affecting less than 2% of daily demand.
PM Wong expects all parties to honour gas supply contracts.
Singapore is boosting LNG imports to diversify energy sources.
The country is studying nuclear energy as a cleaner power option.
Singapore is also strengthening international partnerships.

cards.headline: Singapore haze: Air quality remains unhealthy in three regions; PM2.5 readings normal across country
bullets: Air quality was unhealthy in three areas on Sunday.
South and north air quality dropped out of unhealthy levels.
Hourly PM2.5 readings stayed normal across the country.
Winds and rain might help clear the haze soon.

cards.headline: Why Netflix is struggling to find its audience
bullets: Netflix's sales growth slowed to its weakest in three years.
The company is cutting about 1,000 jobs, or 6% of its staff.
Rivals like YouTube and Apple TV are gaining more viewers.
Netflix hired a new executive to help find more hit shows.

cards.headline: Hyundai Elexio review: The Korean EV built for Chinese tastes
bullets: The Hyundai Elexio uses BYD battery cells, known for safety in Singapore.
This electric car, made in China for Chinese tastes, has a huge 27-inch touchscreen.
It offers a plush interior with lots of space for passengers and a large boot.
The car accelerates slowly, taking 10.7 seconds to reach 100 kmh.
Priced at S$191,999 with COE, it offers a 405 km range and sharp handling.

cards.headline: Net demand for Singapore office space doubles in Q3 as central region rents rise 0.8%
bullets: Office space demand in Singapore doubled in Q3 compared to the previous quarter.
Rents for offices in the central area went up by 0.8% in the last three months.
The overall empty office space rate dropped to 10% as less new space became available.
Tech and finance companies were major drivers of the increased office space demand.

cards.headline: Home sales set to recover in Q4 with prices seen rising further on new launch momentum
bullets: Private home prices rose 1.4% in the last quarter, the fastest in seven quarters.
However, new home sales dropped by nearly half compared to the previous quarter.
More new homes are launching in the next quarter, which should boost sales.
Analysts expect home prices to end the year up 3% to 5%.

cards.headline: KKR founders among investors buying 42% of Peter Lim’s Valencia; club valued at US$1.4 billion
bullets: US investors bought 42% of Valencia football club from Peter Lim's company.
The deal values the Spanish club at US$1.4 billion.
New investors are injecting 100 million euros to help the club.
Peter Lim's company will still own most of Valencia.
The club is currently struggling in Spain's top football league.

cards.headline: Abby Choi murder trial: Cut mark on spine consistent with electric saw blade found in flat where body parts were discovered
bullets: A cut on Abby Choi's spine matched an electric saw found at the crime scene.
Parts of Choi's body, including legs, were found in a refrigerator.
Her head was discovered in pots of soup and minced meat.
Choi's ex-husband's family bought a meat mincer before her death.
The ex-father-in-law admitted buying kitchen tools, including a meat mincer.

cards.headline: S'pore man, 41, & serial voyeur, jailed for 7th time since 2018 after filming upskirt videos at Yishun
bullets: A 41-year-old man was jailed 28 weeks for filming upskirt videos, his seventh jail term since 2018.
He filmed women at Northpoint City and elsewhere, sometimes twice a week.
The judge gave him a longer sentence than prosecutors asked for.
He was warned he could face caning if he offends again.

cards.headline: US woman on 10-hour flight refuses to switch seats with passenger, who then cries for 3 hours as she can't lay her head on husband's shoulder
bullets: A woman refused to give up her aisle seat on a 10-hour flight, causing another passenger to cry.
The other passenger wanted to sit next to her husband but he was in a middle seat two rows ahead.
The crying passenger said she missed her husband and had nowhere to rest her head.
The influencer who filmed the incident was flying home after her father passed away.

cards.headline: Tampines 1’s New Stores & Returning Faves, Plus Special Deals at Level 3
bullets: Tampines 1 mall's Level 3 has new stores and returning favourites.
New shops include Box Hunt for blind boxes and KPOP HOUSE for K-Pop merchandise.
Dessert shop Geláre and claw machine arcade FUNCLAW & ORODOKI also opened.
Awfully Chocolate has a new beverage bar concept at the mall.
Promotions include 1-for-1 deals at Geláre and 8% off at KPOP HOUSE.

cards.headline: 13 Free Loyalty Memberships In Singapore With Freebies, Birthday Treats & Plenty Of Perks
bullets: IKEA Family membership is free for residents aged 18 and above.
Mr. Coconut offers free lifetime membership with a free drink upon signing up.
Yo-Chi's free Chi Club membership gives a $10 birthday voucher with no minimum spend.
Swensen's Cool Rewards offers a free lifetime membership with a birthday sundae.
Join loyalty programmes for freebies, birthday treats, and discounts.

cards.headline: 11 Upcoming Card Shows & Conventions In Singapore To Feed Your TCG Obsession & Hunt For Rare Cards
bullets: Several card shows and conventions are happening in Singapore soon for collectors.
Asia Cards & Collectible Expo runs for six weekends at Suntec City.
SG Collectibles & Card Show has three themed editions in October, November, and December.
NEXUS TCG Tradeshow offers over 50 vendors at The Centrepoint and Suntec.
Award X Halloween Trade Night features prizes and lucky draws for $10 tickets.
